notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My first attempt to fetch the sources failed with an error saying I had no tool calls left for this turn, so I wasn't able to read any of the pages.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have no source material, any verse-by-verse notes I wrote now would come from memory, and I'd have no real URLs to cite. So I've left the notes out.

**What I was going to read:**
- **Traditional reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-27/, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary entries for Isaiah 27 on biblehub.com, and preceptaustin.org's Isaiah 27 page
- **Modern scholarship:** netbible.org's translator notes on Isaiah 27, especially on Leviathan (v. 1), the hard Hebrew in v. 8, and the Asherah poles (v. 9)
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mainly vv. 1, 6 and 12–13. These cover the end-times reading of Leviathan and whether the promises about Israel are about the nation Israel or the church. I'd use Wesley's Notes, Spurgeon, Ligonier/Monergism, LCMS/1517 and pneumareview/samstorms.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** newadvent.org (Church Fathers, Haydock-style notes) and oca.org, if they have anything on this chapter

If you send the request again in a new turn, I'll start by fetching these pages and then write the notes as you asked: verse by verse, each point with its URL, and anything I can't find left out.
